newsitem.title: USA: Minn Twins stadium bill advances in House - paper.
newsitem.headline: Minn Twins stadium bill advances in House - paper.

text.p: A Minnesota House committee late Wednesday revived a newly amended Twins stadium bill on a 12-6 vote, the Star Tribune reported Thursday.
The House Local Government and Metropolitan Affairs Committee decision to advance the proposal increases the chances that the ailing proposal will make it to the House floor, the newspaper reported.

The bill still requires Twins owner Carl Pohlad to contribute $50 million toward the estimated $400 million cost of the proposed retractable roof stadium, $35 million more than he is willing to provide, the newspaper reported.

Committee members adopted several modifications before advancing the bill Wednesday, including limiting a 10 percent sales tax on sports memorabilia to Twins merchandise sold outside the stadium, the newspaper reported.

The bill would also require the sale of the former Met Center site in suburban Minneapolis with the proceeds earmarked to help pay off the remaining debt on the Metrodome where the Twins now play, the newspaper reported.

The bill was also amended to limit a special economic development district around the new stadium and to impose a 4 percent surcharge on Twins and visiting ballplayers who earn more than $100,000 per year.
A Senate committee earlier stripped public financing from a companion bill before advancing that proposal.
